about: Test window, the test split only: test-break session A's A2, recorded after the freeze (8c7b2f6); no replay, sweep, or tuning on it except the test sweep. A db_pool_exhaustion break at 20:57:34 (POOL_MAX_SIZE 20 to 2), left to end with the fault's 390 s lifetime (reverted to 20 at 21:04:05, after the alarms), never cleared by hand, with the alarm rule off: no agent run. Pool wait went into ALARM at 20:58:11, latency at 21:01:38, errors at 21:01:46. Errors was OK at 21:02:06 and into ALARM again at 21:02:26: that repeat is left out of the replays on purpose (the recording's span ends at 21:02:15) and kept in the alarm history only, as earlier windows keep their re-fires. All three were OK by 21:04:18. A distractor in the 180-minute log reach: A1, the bad_deploy break of 19:17:18 (1.43.0's 500s; errors into ALARM 19:17:46, OK 19:24:06), 100 minutes before the onset. The deploy history shows the pool change at 20:57:34, a decoy CART_TTL_HOURS 24 to 48 at 19:31:26, A1's rollback to 1.42.0 at 19:23:49 and its 1.43.0 deploy at 19:17:18, and decoys RECOMMENDATIONS_ENABLED false to true at 18:05:34 and CART_TTL_HOURS 24 to 48 at 16:03:56. One of the decoys at 18:05:34 and 19:31:26 was written by A3's break, after this window's alarms (back-dated 1 to 6 hours; which one is unrecorded), so a live read here would have shown one of them, not both.
account: 123456789012 stands in for the account ID wherever AWS wrote it.
